n: Moroni begins his final chapter, addressing the Lamanites. More than 420 years have passed since the sign of Christ’s birth, so this is around AD 421.

f.w: the sign was given of the coming of Christ

n: Moroni is about to seal up the plates for the last time, but first offers some words of exhortation — earnest encouragement and counsel.
Before asking whether the book is true, readers should remember how merciful God has been to humanity from Adam to their own day, and ponder it deeply. Pondering prepares the heart for revelation.

f.w: remember how merciful the Lord hath been

n: Moroni’s famous promise: ask God the Father in Christ’s name whether these things are true. If you ask sincerely, with real intent and faith in Christ, he will reveal the truth by the Holy Ghost. Many converts point to this verse as the start of their testimony.

f.g: intending to act on the answer, not merely curious.

f.w: he will manifest the truth of it unto you

n: The promise reaches beyond the Book of Mormon: by the Holy Ghost we can know the truth of all things. The same Spirit that witnesses of the book can guide us in every search for truth.
Everything good is also just and true, and nothing good denies Christ; rather, it testifies that he lives. This echoes Mormon’s test for discerning good from evil.

f.w: nothing that is good denieth the Christ

n: The Holy Ghost can witness that Christ lives. Moroni pleads with us not to deny God’s power, which works according to people’s faith and never changes.

f.w: the same today and tomorrow, and forever

n: Moroni urges readers not to deny the many gifts of the Spirit. They take different forms, but all come from the same God for the benefit of his children.

f.w: deny not the gifts of God

n: The list of gifts begins: some receive the ability to teach wisdom — practical, inspired understanding of how to live.

f.g: a spiritual gift of wise teaching; not the same as the health code of D&C 89.

n: Others are given the gift to teach knowledge — to understand and explain truth clearly — by the same Spirit.
Some receive exceptionally great faith; others the gift of healing. Both come from the same Spirit.
Some are given power to work mighty miracles, as many prophets and apostles have done.
Others receive the gift of prophecy — speaking God’s truth and foretelling events by inspiration.
Some are blessed to see angels and ministering spirits. Moroni himself would later be such a messenger to Joseph Smith.
Others receive the gift of speaking in various tongues — including the ability to learn and speak languages to share the gospel.
Still others can interpret languages and tongues. Together these gifts allow the gospel to reach every nation.
All these gifts come through the Spirit of Christ, given to each person individually as he chooses. No one has every gift, and everyone has some.
Moroni reminds us that every good gift comes from Christ — a fitting summary of his father’s teachings.

f.w: every good gift cometh of Christ

n: Christ is unchanging, so these spiritual gifts will never be taken away as long as the world lasts — unless people lose them through unbelief.

f.w: the same yesterday, today, and forever

n: Moroni links faith, hope, and charity in a chain: each requires the next. He echoes his father’s great sermon in chapter 7.
Without charity, faith, and hope, no one can be saved in God’s kingdom. All three are essential.

f.g: in no way; not at all.

n: Without hope, people fall into despair — and despair comes from sin. Hope in Christ is the remedy.
Moroni repeats Christ’s promise to the Nephites: with faith, they can do all that is needful in Christ’s eyes.

f.w: If ye have faith ye can do all things which are expedient unto me

n: Speaking now to the whole world, Moroni warns that if God’s power and gifts ever disappear from a people, it will be because of their unbelief.

f.w: it shall be because of unbelief

n: That would be a tragic condition, for no one would do good at all. Anyone who truly does good works by God’s power and gifts.
Those who reject God’s gifts and die without repenting die in their sins. Moroni insists he speaks Christ’s words and tells the truth.

Moroni says we will meet him at God’s judgment bar, where God will ask whether we heeded words written by one “crying from the dead” and “speaking out of the dust” — a description of the Book of Mormon coming forth from the ground.

f.g: the place of judgment, pictured as a courtroom bar.

n: These words fulfill prophecy. God’s word will “hiss forth” — be called out like a signal — to every generation.

f.g: to whistle or call out as a signal to gather; an image from Isaiah.

n: Moroni’s confidence is simple: God himself will confirm that what he wrote is true.
His last great invitation: come unto Christ, grasp every good gift, and avoid every evil and unclean thing.

f.w: touch not the evil gift, nor the unclean thing

n: Moroni draws on Isaiah’s images of Zion awakening, dressing in beautiful garments, and spreading its tent with strengthened stakes. Latter-day Saints see this fulfilled in the gathering of Israel and the growth of the Church.

f.w: arise from the dust, O Jerusalem
strengthen thy stakes and enlarge thy borders

f.g: put to shame; thrown into confusion.

n: One of the great verses on grace: come to Christ, give up ungodliness, and love God with all your heart, and his grace is enough to make you perfect in him. Perfection is not something we achieve alone but a gift through Christ.

f.w: love God with all your might, mind and strength
then is his grace sufficient for you

n: Those made perfect in Christ are sanctified — made holy and spotless — through the shedding of his blood, as promised in the Father’s covenant for forgiving sins.

f.g: made holy; cleansed and set apart for God.

n: Moroni bids farewell, expecting soon to rest in paradise until his resurrection. He will meet us before “the pleasing bar of the great Jehovah” — Christ, the Judge of the living and the dead. About fourteen centuries later he returned as an angel to Joseph Smith.

f.g: Latter-day Saints understand Jehovah as the premortal name of Jesus Christ.
quick = living; the living and the dead.
